title.narrative: Affordable and Sustainable Energy Transition Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative:
The Affordable and Sustainable Energy Transition Program will support the Government of Indonesia in achieving its enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), 2022 and its power subsector net-zero emission target by 2050 through various policy measures to accelerate energy transition in the country. The program is a milestone intervention in Indonesia's shift of focus from securing energy supply to a transition to clean energy for sustainable growth. It leverages the momentum created by Indonesia's climate and energy transition commitments made in 2022. The program will be designed to align well with the climate focus of Asian Development Bank's (ADB's) country partnership strategy for Indonesia, 2020-2024 and the principles of ADB's Energy Policy. It also seeks to contribute to three operational priorities of ADB's Strategy 2030 : accelerating progress in gender equality, tackling climate change, and strengthening governance and institutional capacity.
The program will be a programmatic approach policy-based lending (PBL) with two subprograms. However, the reform actions may require a third subprogram, which will be determined during subprogram 2 preparation. Energy transition requires a multiyear staggering of reform actions and a programmatic approach rather than a single PBL.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. The government has issued the CIPP 2023-2030 as the detailed decarbonization and energy transition action plan for Indonesia to achieve its 2030 greenhouse gas emissions target of capping the on-grid emissions at 250 million tons of CO2 including priority investment and financing plans for scaling up renewable energy capacity and early retirement of coal-fired power plants, strategy to ensure a just energy transition considering the socioeconomic impact, including on gender equality, enabling policy options and implementation framework. (CMMI)

1.2. CMMI has issued a decision to establish the government's minister-level energy transition task force to supervise and monitor energy transition activities centrally, including activities stipulated in the CIPP. (CMMI)

1.3. CMMI has issued a decree to establish a working team, consisting of senior management officials of CMMI, other related ministries and PLN, that regularly reports to the national energy transition taskforce to ensure implementation of energy transition activities with focus areas aligned with the CIPP. (CMMI)

1.4. MEMR has approved and issued a regulation, eliminating capacity fees and establishing procedures to set the system quota of distributed electricity generation activities, especially for commercial and industrial sectors to increase the number of rooftop solar PV facility installations in Indonesia. (MEMR)

1.5. MEMR has issued a ministerial regulation to establish the basis for carbon trading with emissions from coal-fired power plants connected to the PLN power systems as the initial priority, and a decree to assign emission ceiling to each power plant as an initial step of implementing a carbon trading market. d (MEMR)
1.6. MEMR has issued a regulation providing incentives to accelerate the deployment of up to 50,000 units in 2023 and 150,000 units in 2024 of electric two-wheelers in the country. (MEMR)

1.7. The Ministry of Finance has issued a regulation to set up the Energy Transition Platform for providing financing, including blended financing and international financial institution financing for energy transition investments including early retirement of coal-fired power plants and their replacement with renewable energy.

Action 1: Pertamina and PLN have improved their risk reporting by preparing and publishing (i) in the case of PLN, a risk management monitoring and activities report for 2024 which includes the impact of climate change on the reliability of the electricity system; and (ii) in the case of Pertamina, by preparing and publishing a Sustainability Report in 2022 that includes a description of various risks associated with climate change and of the related mitigation measures. (Pertamina and PLN)
Action 2: Pertamina Geothermal Energy has completed its initial public offering of 25% of its shares which will help increase transparency and governance of the agency's operations as well as to provide additional financial resources for its geothermal investments. (Pertamina)
Action 3: PLN has completed a corporate reorganization into a holding and sub-holding structure to consolidate specific areas of power supply activities to each subsidiary to improve efficiency and agility in its operations. (PLN)
Action 4: PLN has approved (i) a Legal and Human Resources Directors' Instruction to respond to changes in work culture and support diversity and inclusion within the organization, including availability of facilities for childcare; (ii) a technical instruction on Respectful Workplace by President Director to promote an inclusive workplace free of discrimination, violence, and harassment, to drive corporate sustainability, explicitly addressing the protection and prevention of sexual harassment within the organization; and (iii) updates to its Statement of Corporate Intent on Gender Equality, spelling out actions to guide and increase corporate capacity for gender mainstreaming across key corporate functions, including human resources, procurement, gender focal point system, education and training, and monitoring and reporting.e
Action 1: The government will approve a mechanism to incorporate the result of a nationwide survey to confirm the eligibility of subsidy recipients to improve the targeting of electricity subsidies.
Action 2: Energy sector state-owned enterprises will implement the guidelines provided by MSOE and report on sustainability indices based on international best practices.
Action 3: PLN will implement priority technical and financial reforms set out in CIPP to achieve the government's target emissions reduction
Action 4: PLN conducts a corporate gender assessment, approves corporate gender mainstreaming standard operating procedure, defines performance indicators to promote gender equality, and pursues corporate certification for gender equality, diversity and inclusion.
